S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents involving injury, property damage, or a safety-related shutdown. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours of learning of an incident involving their unit, and promptly notify other customers of the same model when the incident indicates a model-level safety risk.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and a statistically representative sample. Manufacturers shall submit per-model results to the relevant regulator and provide results to customers on request; individual-company per-model failure rates shall not be published publicly. A result above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a corrective-action and retesting plan, but is not by itself grounds for an automatic sales ban.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a means for the customer to verify shut-off status. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within 6 years after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression designed to control or contain a battery fire without creating an additional hazard. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A model exceeding 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year triggers prompt regulator notification, a public customer notice, and an expedited model-specific safety assessment. The exceedance alone does not automatically require a recall: the regulator shall determine whether a recall or other corrective action is necessary based on incident severity, exposure, test results, and the effectiveness of alternatives. A recall is mandatory when the regulator determines that a model presents an unacceptable safety risk that cannot be adequately mitigated by less restrictive action.

document.section_notes: S1 is safe with 24h regulator reporting, 3-day customer notice, and all-incident scope. S2 is weakened because the 5% failure rate only triggers corrective action and no automatic sales ban, with public per-model rates withheld. S3 and S4 are acceptable (6-year retrofit, 36-month suppression). S5 is weakened: the 8/100k trigger leads to assessment, but recall is discretionary and corrective action can replace it indefinitely.
